lesson_title: Map Scale: Your Ruler Measures the Landscape
hook_text: Your 30cm ruler can measure 15km of South Africa. Here's the trick.
clip_script: Read it literally: one unit of any length on the map represents fifty thousand of those same units on the ground. One centimetre on paper is 50 000 centimetres of real South Africa. Get a feel for the size: 50 000 centimetres is 500 metres, half a kilometre. So on a 1:50 000 sheet, every centimetre of paper is half a kilometre of ground. Two centimetres, one kilometre. A ruler laid across the map is literally measuring the landscape.
visual_style: Ruler laid on a topographic map dissolving into a drone shot of the same terrain, distance labels flying from paper to landscape.
pacing: Snappy hook, one clean idea unfolding, confident finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and turn 8,6 cm into 4,3 km in four lines.
